title: Walkthrough II: context, memory and extensibility
takeaway: Choose what persists, what executes, and what can leave the machine.

sentences.text: In omp, a long-running checkout task crosses several information boundaries: what the model sees now, what persists later, and what integrations execute.
Project instructions, always-carried rules, on-demand skills, and cross-session memory serve different lifetimes; choose the mechanism to match the information.
Native project discovery stops at the nearest nonempty configuration directory, which can block instructions farther up the tree.
Keep always-carried requirements short, and inspect the discovered sources before assuming the project instructions loaded.

Use terminal Injecting rule wording with rewind glyph and italic rule description; this live-notice shape is source-derived, not a resumed captured event. 10.2.2 diagram separates regex streaming and AST pre-execution lanes. 10.2.3 begin the judged lane only after completed output; keep judge prerequisites visible. 10.2.4 separate correction from execution containment.

sentences.text: Time Traveling Stream Rules can interrupt a matching streamed attempt, inject corrective guidance, and retry; the facility is enabled by default.
Regex rules can match during streaming, while AST rules inspect finalized source-bearing tool arguments before execution.
Judged question rules wait for completed output, so they cannot interrupt the stream; their judge must also be available.
Use this for corrective guidance, not as the security boundary around tool execution.

Do not show cost, token or timing measurements. 10.3.1 type /compact and use diagram summary plus recent tail, preserving the visible transcript lane. 10.3.2 turn older coupon-investigation text into bounded schematic raster tiles without token-savings counters. 10.3.3 retain the downstream-image-cost label. 10.3.4 type the focused /handoff from 10.3.c and keep the same session identity tile.

sentences.text: As the checkout investigation grows, compaction reduces model-visible history to a summary and recent tail while preserving visible scrollback.
Snapcompact instead renders older text into images locally, without a summarization model; the next model must support vision.
That image archive is bounded and can be truncated, and reading it later still incurs the provider’s image costs.
For a focused continuation, handoff generates a document within the same session rather than creating another agent.

Do not show cost, token or timing measurements. 10.4.1 use diagram backend capability matrix; terminal contains an unsubmitted /memory stats. 10.4.2 separate local storage from processing/network arrows. 10.4.3 keep structured retain/recall tools absent from the local-summary row; use the fixture lesson "Expiry is inclusive" as an explicitly illustrative memory card, not a retrieved service result. 10.4.4 send that lesson back through a current-source check.

sentences.text: Cross-session memory is opt-in, with five documented modes including off: local summaries, Hindsight, Mnemopi, and Sharpshooter.
Hindsight needs a reachable server; Mnemopi keeps local databases, but its default processing route can use an online model.
Separate storage from processing: the local summary backend has no structured memory tools, and a local database does not imply offline inference.
Treat a remembered coupon policy as a lead to verify against current source, not a permanent authority.

sentences.text: Session history is a tree: return to an earlier checkout decision while ordinary branching preserves the alternative path.
Tree navigation stays in the same session file; forking creates a new identity and, in persistent mode, a new file.
Active context follows the selected ancestry; separate pruning and destructive rewrite operations can remove history.

Coupons fixture: inclusive expiry / alternative policy branches
Ordinary branch: same session, prior branch retained
/fork: new identity/file in persistent mode
Pruning and destructive helpers are separate

sentences.text: Plan mode gives the checkout change a review boundary, but fresh sessions do not enter it automatically.
Prewalk is separate and off by default: it switches models after an eligible edit or write result, at the completed-turn boundary.
The starting model may already have edited code before handing over the task.

Do not show cost, token or timing measurements. 10.7.1 show compact Read skill://coupon-review; diagram expands instruction text separately from an executable function. 10.7.2 add MCP bridge and server-instructions toggle, without launching a server. 10.7.3 highlight executable extension loading as a code-trust boundary.

sentences.text: Skills supply instructions, tools execute functions, and extensions register capabilities or intercept lifecycle events; modern hook files use that extension runtime.
MCP connects external tools, resources, and prompts, adding server-controlled instructions as another trust surface.
Loading an executable extension means trusting its code, not simply adding a page of guidance.

sentences.text: Secret obfuscation is off by default and partial when enabled; static prompts, static tool definitions, and binaries fall outside its boundary.
HTML exports can contain raw context, so review what a working session contains before sharing it.
Choose deliberately what persists, what executes, and what can leave the machine.

onScreen.text:
secrets.enabled=false
When enabled: selective reversible text substitution, not universal redaction
Excluded: static prompts · static tool definitions · binaries · opaque encrypted replay
